requirements: The core contributions of the paper 'Quest: Query-Aware Sparsity for Efficient Long-Context LLM Inference' have been reproduced, including the query-aware KV cache page selection algorithm, its CUDA kernel implementation, and the accuracy/efficiency evaluations demonstrating up to 7.03× self-attention speedup and 2.23× end-to-end latency reduction with negligible accuracy loss.

sub_tasks.requirements: The long-context models (LongChat-7b-v1.5-32k, Yarn-Llama-2-7b-128k, Llama2-7B) and the evaluation datasets (PG19, passkey retrieval, six LongBench datasets: NarrativeQA, HotpotQA, Qasper, TriviaQA, GovReport, MultiFieldQA) are downloaded, prepared, and ready for evaluation.
The three long-context language models used across Quest's accuracy and efficiency experiments are downloaded and loadable in FP16 with tokenizers and generation configs intact.

Code has been implemented that downloads or resolves the LongChat-7b-v1.5-32k model checkpoint (e.g. from HuggingFace `lmsys/longchat-7b-v1.5-32k`) into a local cache directory and exposes the local path used by all PG19, 10k passkey, and LongBench experiments.

verification.spec: Run the download/resolve script; assert that the local path exists, contains the LongChat-7b-v1.5-32k config.json with model_type=llama, and that a documented environment variable / path variable exposes it.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that downloads or resolves the Yarn-Llama-2-7b-128k model checkpoint (e.g. from HuggingFace `NousResearch/Yarn-Llama-2-7b-128k`) into a local cache directory and exposes the local path used by the 100k passkey retrieval experiment.

verification.spec: Run the download/resolve script; assert that the local path exists, contains the Yarn-Llama-2-7b-128k config.json indicating 128k context and RoPE scaling, and that the path is exposed via a documented variable.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that downloads or resolves the Llama2-7B base checkpoint used for the kernel-level and end-to-end efficiency evaluations (Sec 4.3.1 and 4.3.2) and exposes it via a documented local path.

verification.spec: Run the download/resolve script; assert that the local path exists, contains a Llama-2-7b HF config (model_type=llama, hidden_size=4096, num_hidden_layers=32), and is exposed via a documented path variable.

sub_tasks.requirements: A loader utility exists that returns each of the three models in FP16 with its matching tokenizer and rotary position embedding / context-length configuration preserved (LongChat 32k, Yarn-Llama-2 128k, Llama2-7B), and a smoke test forwards a short prompt through each model without shape or dtype errors.

verification.spec: Call the loader for each of LongChat-7b-v1.5-32k, Yarn-Llama-2-7b-128k, and Llama-2-7B; verify dtype is FP16, tokenizer is returned, `config.max_position_embeddings` (or RoPE scaling config) matches expected context (32k, 128k, 4k), and forward a short prompt to obtain logits without error.

sub_tasks.requirements: The PG19 language-modeling test set used in Section 4.2.1 is downloaded and prepared into contiguous 32k-token slices from the PG19 test books, ready for the perplexity sweep from 0 to 32000 input tokens.

Code has been implemented that downloads the PG19 test split (100 books, average ~70k tokens) — for example via the `pg19` HuggingFace dataset or the DeepMind release — into a local cache directory used by the PG19 evaluation.

verification.spec: Run a script that loads the PG19 test split via `datasets.load_dataset('deepmind/pg19', split='test')` or equivalent; assert len(dataset) == 100 and mean token length across the split is >= 50000 tokens using the LongChat tokenizer.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that tokenizes each PG19 test book with the LongChat-7b-v1.5-32k tokenizer and yields fixed-length windows up to 32000 tokens so perplexity can be evaluated at input lengths from 0 to 32000 as in Fig. 6.

verification.spec: Invoke the PG19 window-generator: it should tokenize a PG19 test book with the LongChat-7b-v1.5-32k tokenizer and yield windows whose token lengths span from small (~0) up to 32000. Assert at least one window has exactly 32000 tokens and windows for lengths 0, 5000, 10000, 15000, 20000, 25000, 30000, 32000 can be produced (matching Fig. 6 sweep).

sub_tasks.requirements: A verification test asserts the loaded PG19 test set contains 100 books and that after tokenization at least one full 32000-token window is available for perplexity evaluation.

verification.spec: Load the PG19 test split via the project's loader; assert len(books) == 100. Tokenize the longest book with the LongChat tokenizer and assert token count >= 32000 so at least one 32000-token window exists.

sub_tasks.requirements: Quest's criticality estimation logic (per-page min/max Key metadata maintenance, channel-wise upper-bound attention score U_i = max(Q_i*m_i, Q_i*M_i), sum-reduction across dimensions, Top-K page selection) has been implemented as specified in Algorithm 1 and Section 3.4.
Per-page Key metadata (channel-wise min vector m and max vector M) is stored and updated as new tokens are inserted into the KV cache, matching the insertion loop in Algorithm 1.
Code has been implemented to allocate a per-page metadata tensor pair (m_i, M_i) of shape [num_pages, head_dim] (or [num_pages, num_heads, head_dim] for multi-head) alongside the KV cache pages.

verification.spec: Instantiate the KV cache manager for a given num_pages, num_heads, head_dim, and inspect that a metadata tensor pair (m_i, M_i) is allocated with the expected shape [num_pages, num_heads, head_dim] (or [num_pages, head_dim] documented equivalent), and dtype matches the KV dtype.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that M_i is initialized to -inf (or the smallest representable value) and m_i is initialized to +inf before any Key is inserted, so element-wise max/min updates behave correctly on the first token.

verification.spec: Allocate a fresh page's metadata via the initializer and assert that M_i tensor equals -inf (or dtype min) and m_i tensor equals +inf (or dtype max) across all channels, so first-insertion max/min updates are correct.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that, on each new Key insertion k, performs the element-wise updates M_i = max(M_i, k_i) and m_i = min(m_i, k_i) across all head_dim channels for the page the token belongs to (Algorithm 1, insert branch).

verification.spec: Insert two synthetic Key vectors k1, k2 into a page via the insertion API; assert M_i == elementwise_max(init_M, k1, k2) and m_i == elementwise_min(init_m, k1, k2) across all head_dim channels within FP tolerance.

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test inserts a synthetic sequence of Key vectors into a fresh page and asserts that the resulting m_i and M_i tensors equal the per-channel min and max of the inserted vectors within floating-point tolerance.

verification.spec: Generate a random synthetic sequence of N=16 Key vectors of dim=128, insert them into a fresh page via the metadata updater, and assert torch.allclose(m_i, keys.min(0)) and torch.allclose(M_i, keys.max(0)) within 1e-5 tolerance.

sub_tasks.requirements: The channel-wise upper-bound attention score U_i = max(Q_i * m_i, Q_i * M_i) is implemented as specified in Section 3.4 so that U_i upper-bounds Q_i * K_i for every K in the page regardless of the sign of Q_i.

Code has been implemented that computes both Q_i * m_i and Q_i * M_i channel-wise for each page and then takes their element-wise maximum to form U_i, matching the MAX(q_i*max, q_i*min) line of Algorithm 1.

verification.spec: Call the criticality-estimation function with a fixed Q, m_i, M_i, then verify that the intermediate per-channel U_i tensor equals torch.maximum(Q * m_i, Q * M_i) elementwise within FP tolerance.

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test with an all-positive Q vector, an all-positive Key page, and known m_i, M_i verifies that U_i equals Q_i * M_i element-wise (the positive-Q case).

verification.spec: Build a test with all-positive Q, all-positive Keys in a page (so m_i, M_i > 0). Compute U_i via Quest and assert U_i is close to Q * M_i elementwise within 1e-6 tolerance.

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test with an all-negative Q vector verifies that U_i equals Q_i * m_i element-wise, confirming the sign-flip case is handled correctly.

verification.spec: Build a test with all-negative Q and mixed Keys with known m_i, M_i. Compute U_i via Quest and assert U_i is close to Q * m_i elementwise (since negative Q times smaller value yields the larger product) within 1e-6 tolerance.

sub_tasks.requirements: A property-based test with mixed-sign random Q, K tensors and a random page assignment asserts that for every token in the page and every channel i, Q_i * K_i <= U_i (the upper-bound property that underpins Quest's approximation), across at least 100 randomized trials.

verification.spec: Run 100 random trials, each generating Q and K page (mixed-sign) of size [S=16, dim=128]; insert Ks to build m_i, M_i; compute U_i; assert that for all tokens k in page and all channels i, Q[i] * k[i] <= U_i[i] + 1e-6. Failures should raise.

sub_tasks.requirements: Per-page criticality scores are produced by summing the channel-wise upper bounds U_i over all head_dim channels, matching the score accumulation in Algorithm 1 and the 'Sum' step in Figure 5.
Code has been implemented that reduces U_i across the head_dim axis with a sum reduction, producing one scalar criticality score per page (per attention head).

verification.spec: Call criticality estimation with a known U_i and assert the returned score tensor equals U_i.sum(dim=-1) (sum reduction across head_dim) within FP tolerance, and that the score has one scalar per (head, page).

sub_tasks.requirements: The criticality-score tensor returned by the estimation kernel has shape [num_heads, num_pages] (or an equivalent transposed layout documented in the code) so that Top-K can be applied per head.

verification.spec: Call the criticality-estimation kernel with num_heads=32, num_pages=8, and assert the returned tensor shape is (32, 8) or a documented transposed equivalent (8, 32), suitable for per-head Top-K reduction.

sub_tasks.requirements: Top-K page selection is applied to the per-page criticality scores to return the indices of the K pages with the highest estimated upper-bound attention, matching the Top-K step in Figure 5.

Code has been implemented that, given a criticality-score tensor and a hyper-parameter K, returns the indices of the K largest scores per head (using RAFT batched Top-K, torch.topk, or an equivalent primitive documented in the code).

verification.spec: Given a synthetic score tensor of shape [num_heads=4, num_pages=32] and K=8, call the Top-K selector and assert the returned index tensor has shape [4, 8] and, for each head row, its indices correspond to the 8 largest scores in that row (verified against torch.topk).

sub_tasks.requirements: The Top-K page selector exposes K (equivalently, a 'token budget' B = K * page_size) as a configurable argument so that the paper's reported budgets (32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096) can be swept without code changes.

verification.spec: Call the top-K selector / attention entry point with token_budget values in {32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096} via a public config argument (no code edits); assert each call succeeds and the number of selected pages equals ceil(budget/page_size).

sub_tasks.requirements: When the number of pages currently in the KV cache is less than or equal to K, the selector returns all page indices rather than erroring or duplicating pages.

verification.spec: Populate a KV cache with num_pages=4 pages and call the selector with K=8; assert the returned index tensor contains exactly 4 unique valid indices (no duplicates, no error), covering all existing pages.

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test compares the estimator+Top-K output against a brute-force reference (compute full Q*K per page, take the max within each page, take Top-K) on synthetic data and confirms that recall of the reference Top-K pages by Quest's Top-K pages is 100% when K equals the number of pages and is monotonic in K.

verification.spec: Generate synthetic Q, K for N pages; compute the brute-force reference (full Q*K, per-page max, then torch.topk) and Quest's estimator+Top-K output; assert recall of the reference Top-K set is 100% when K==num_pages, and record recall as K decreases to confirm monotonic non-increase.

sub_tasks.requirements: The criticality estimator operates on PageAttention-style page-granular KV cache with a configurable page size S, matching Section 3.4's reliance on Kwon et al. (2023) PagedAttention and Section 3.5's memory-movement analysis.

Code has been implemented so that page size S is a module-level or config-level constant (defaulting to 16 as stated in Section 3.5) and the metadata layout, estimator, and Top-K all consume the same S.

verification.spec: Import the Quest module and locate the page-size constant (e.g., PAGE_SIZE or config.page_size). Assert its default equals 16. Verify the metadata allocator, estimator, and Top-K all read the same constant (grep or import the same symbol) rather than each hard-coding 16 independently.

sub_tasks.requirements: A behavioral test with S=16 and a 256-token synthetic sequence confirms that the criticality estimator produces exactly ceil(256/16)=16 page scores per head.

verification.spec: With page_size S=16 and a synthetic sequence of 256 tokens (single head), populate the KV cache and call the criticality estimator; assert the returned per-page score tensor has exactly ceil(256/16)=16 entries per head.

sub_tasks.requirements: The first two decoder layers use full dense attention (no criticality-based pruning) as prescribed in Section 3.4 due to their low sparsity ratio.
Code has been implemented that gates Quest's estimator+Top-K path on layer_idx, so that when layer_idx < 2 the model falls back to the dense self-attention kernel and otherwise uses Quest.

verification.spec: Import the Quest attention module and instantiate it with a mock model. Monkey-patch or spy on both the dense attention kernel and the Quest estimator+Top-K path. Invoke the attention forward with layer_idx=0 and layer_idx=1 and assert only the dense kernel is called and the Quest estimator is NOT called. Then invoke with layer_idx=2, 5, and 15 and assert the Quest estimator+Top-K path IS called for each. Confirm outputs for layers 0-1 numerically match a reference dense attention within fp16 tolerance.

sub_tasks.requirements: The number of skipped initial layers is exposed as a configuration parameter (defaulting to 2) so that ablations can toggle it, per the paper's note that layer skipping is orthogonal to the KV cache selection algorithm.

verification.spec: Instantiate the Quest attention module / config without specifying the skip-layers parameter and assert the default is 2. Then instantiate with explicit values of 0, 2, and 4 and verify that (a) the config attribute is set correctly, and (b) the forward pass gates the Quest path such that layers with index < skip_layers use dense attention and layers with index >= skip_layers use Quest. Use a spy on the dense vs Quest code paths to confirm gating behavior tracks the parameter.

sub_tasks.requirements: The end-to-end criticality-estimation pipeline (metadata update on insert -> per-page U_i computation on query -> sum reduction -> Top-K page indices) is composed exactly as depicted in Figure 5 and Algorithm 1.

A single entry-point function (e.g. `estimate_top_k_pages(Q, page_min, page_max, K)`) exists that chains element-wise product with min/max keys, per-channel element-wise max, sum-reduction over channels, and Top-K over pages, returning page indices consumable by the Stage-2 sparse attention kernel.

verification.spec: Import the estimator entry-point function (e.g. estimate_top_k_pages). Construct small synthetic tensors: Q of shape (num_heads, head_dim), page_min and page_max of shape (num_pages, num_heads, head_dim) with num_pages=8, K=3. Call the function and assert it returns a tensor/array of page indices with shape (num_heads, K). Verify correctness by computing the reference score manually: for each page, score = sum over channels of max(Q*page_min, Q*page_max), then compare returned Top-K indices against torch.topk on the reference scores. Also confirm the function chains all four operations (element-wise product with min AND max, per-channel element-wise max, sum-reduction, Top-K) by checking intermediate shapes or by mocking sub-ops.

sub_tasks.requirements: An integration test constructs a mini KV cache of a few pages, runs the metadata-update path on synthetic Keys, then runs the estimate-top-k path and confirms that the returned indices are exactly those selected by a NumPy reference implementation of Algorithm 1.

verification.spec: Build a mini KV cache of 8 pages (page_size=16, head_dim=128) with synthetic Keys inserted via the metadata-update path; then call estimate_top_k with K=3 and Q; independently compute the same via a NumPy reference of Algorithm 1; assert returned index sets are exactly equal.

sub_tasks.requirements: Quantitative properties of the criticality estimator are measured and match the paper's characterization of Quest's approximation.

Across at least 1000 randomized (Q, page-of-K) trials with head_dim=128 and page_size=16, the per-page sum of U_i is measured to be greater than or equal to the true maximum attention logit Q·K over tokens in the page in 100% of trials, empirically confirming the upper-bound property claimed in Section 3.4.

verification.spec: Generate 1000 random (Q, page-of-K) trials with head_dim=128 and page_size=16; compute per-page sum of U_i (Quest score) and true max attention logit Q·K across the page's tokens; assert score >= true_max for all 1000 trials.

sub_tasks.requirements: For a fixed 32K-token synthetic KV cache with a known dense attention distribution, the measured recall of true Top-K page ids by Quest's estimator (averaged over 100 random Q vectors) is at least 0.9 for K equal to 25% of pages, providing a numerical sanity check on the 'closely aligns with oracle' claim of Section 3.4/Fig 3 at the algorithm-only level.

verification.spec: Build a synthetic KV cache of 32K tokens (page_size=16, head_dim=128); for 100 random Q vectors, compute both (a) true Top-K pages by dense softmax attention aggregated per page, and (b) Quest estimator Top-K pages, with K = 25% of pages. Report mean recall of true Top-K among Quest's Top-K.

sub_tasks.requirements: Quest's two-stage sparse self-attention operator is built on top of a PageAttention KV cache: Stage 1 emits per-page criticality scores, Top-K page indices are selected, and Stage 2 performs approximate attention that sparsely loads only the selected pages. The operator honors the page-granularity KV layout, exposes a configurable token budget, and skips Quest on the first two model layers as specified in Section 3.4.
The paged KV cache data structure used by Quest matches PageAttention semantics and exposes per-page K/V tensors plus the min/max Key metadata slots that Stage 1 consumes.
Code has been implemented that defines a PagedKVCache-like container which stores the KV cache as an ordered list of fixed-size pages compatible with FlashInfer's PageAttention layout.

verification.spec: Import the PagedKVCache class from the Quest module. Instantiate it and verify it exposes an ordered indexable page container (e.g., .pages list or .get_page(i) method). Add tokens and verify that pages fill sequentially with fixed page_size. Verify the K/V tensor layout matches FlashInfer's PagedKVCache expected shape (kv_data with layout [num_pages, 2, page_size, num_kv_heads, head_dim] or similar).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that each page holds K and V tensors of shape (page_size, num_kv_heads, head_dim) with dtype matching the model (FP16 for the paper's setting).

verification.spec: Instantiate the PagedKVCache with page_size=16, num_kv_heads=32, head_dim=128, dtype=torch.float16. Insert one page's worth of K and V. Assert the K tensor for that page has shape (16, 32, 128) and dtype torch.float16, and similarly for V.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that allocates a per-page min-Key and max-Key metadata tensor (channel-wise vectors of shape (num_kv_heads, head_dim)) alongside each page for Stage 1 criticality estimation.

verification.spec: Instantiate a PagedKVCache with page_size=16, num_kv_heads=8, head_dim=128. Append 16 random Key vectors. Query the min/max metadata for the page and assert shape (num_kv_heads, head_dim) = (8, 128), and values equal element-wise min/max of the appended Keys within atol=1e-5.

sub_tasks.requirements: The page size S is a configurable parameter of the sparse attention operator and defaults to 16 KV pairs per page, matching the value used in Section 3.5 and the kernel evaluation in Section 4.3.1.

verification.spec: Import the sparse-attention operator constructor and inspect its signature/config: assert a page-size parameter exists and its default value equals 16.

sub_tasks.requirements: Stage 1 of the operator produces a per-page criticality score vector and feeds it to a Top-K page selector that returns exactly K page indices, with K derived from the configured token budget.
Code has been implemented so that Stage 1 returns a criticality score tensor of shape (num_kv_heads, num_pages) computed from the current Query and each page's min/max Key metadata.

verification.spec: Populate a PagedKVCache with 64 tokens (4 pages @ page_size=16), num_kv_heads=8, head_dim=128. Pass a query vector Q of shape (8, 128) through Stage 1. Assert the returned criticality tensor has shape (8, 4).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that invokes a batched Top-K routine on the criticality scores and returns exactly K = ceil(token_budget / page_size) page indices per head.

verification.spec: Populate PagedKVCache with 512 tokens at page_size=16 (32 pages). Run Stage 1 to get scores of shape (num_heads, 32), then invoke the batched Top-K wrapper with token_budget=256 -> K=16. Assert returned tensor has shape (num_heads, 16) of int32/int64 page indices, all indices in range [0, 32).

sub_tasks.requirements: The token budget is exposed as an inference-time hyperparameter of the Quest attention operator so that values used in the paper (64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096) can be swept without code changes.

verification.spec: Import the Quest attention operator and, for each budget B in {64,128,256,512,1024,2048,4096}, instantiate it with token_budget=B; assert no exception is raised and the stored budget attribute equals B without any code modification between runs.

sub_tasks.requirements: Stage 2 of the operator consumes the Top-K page indices, sparsely loads only those pages from the paged KV cache, and computes approximate self-attention whose output has the same shape/dtype as dense attention.
Code has been implemented so that Stage 2 receives the Top-K page-index tensor from Stage 1 and passes it as the sparse loading indices to the approximate PageAttention kernel.

verification.spec: Monkey-patch the approximate PageAttention kernel to record its `page_indices` argument. Run Quest's two-stage attention. Assert the page_indices argument received by Stage 2 is exactly the tensor returned by Stage 1's Top-K step (torch.equal).

sub_tasks.requirements: Only the K selected pages are materialized/read during Stage 2 (not the full KV cache); a unit test asserts that pages outside the Top-K set are never touched (e.g. by wrapping the cache in a read-tracking proxy).

verification.spec: Wrap the PagedKVCache in a proxy that records every page index read during Stage 2. Configure token_budget=64 with page_size=16 (K=4) and populate 16 total pages. Run Stage 2 with a fixed Top-K index set {2, 5, 9, 12}. Assert the proxy recorded reads only for pages {2, 5, 9, 12} and no reads for the other 12 pages.

sub_tasks.requirements: The Quest sparse attention operator returns an output tensor with the same shape and dtype as the FlashInfer dense attention baseline for the same Q/KV inputs.

verification.spec: Run FlashInfer dense attention with Q, K, V and record output tensor's shape and dtype. Run Quest sparse attention on same Q with paged K, V and K=all_pages. Assert output.shape and output.dtype match the FlashInfer output exactly.

sub_tasks.requirements: When the token budget is set high enough that K equals the number of pages (all pages selected), the Quest sparse attention output matches dense FlashInfer attention on the same Q/KV within FP16 numerical tolerance (max abs diff < 1e-2).

verification.spec: Configure Quest sparse attention with K equal to the total number of pages (so all pages are selected); run on the same Q/K/V as a dense FlashInfer call; assert torch.max(torch.abs(quest_out - flashinfer_out)) < 1e-2 in FP16.

sub_tasks.requirements: Page-index sparse loading correctly addresses the paged cache in the presence of edge cases such as partial last pages and non-multiple-of-page-size sequence lengths.

Code has been implemented so that page indices are passed as an integer tensor (int32 or int64) into the approximate attention kernel and used to gather K/V pages via paged addressing rather than a dense contiguous copy.

verification.spec: Inspect the approximate attention kernel's signature via introspection or docstring. Assert the page-indices argument accepts torch.int32 or torch.int64 tensors. Call the kernel with a page_indices tensor and verify K/V are gathered via indexed paged addressing (e.g., kv_data[page_indices]) rather than a contiguous slice/copy; assert the source code contains an indexing or gather operation over page indices.

sub_tasks.requirements: The operator correctly handles sequence lengths that are not a multiple of the page size (the last page is partially filled) and masks the unfilled slots so they do not contribute to attention.

verification.spec: Populate PagedKVCache with 20 tokens at page_size=16 (2 pages; second page has 4 valid tokens and 12 unfilled slots). Compare Quest's approximate attention output (with all pages selected) against a dense reference computed on only the 20 valid tokens. Assert allclose with atol=1e-3. Additionally, corrupt the unfilled slots with NaN and re-run; assert output contains no NaNs (masked out).

sub_tasks.requirements: Following Section 3.4, Quest and all KV-selection baselines are disabled on the first two transformer layers, which fall back to full FlashInfer attention, while Quest is applied from layer index 2 onward.
The number of layers skipped by Quest is exposed as a configuration parameter (e.g. num_skip_layers) whose default value is 2, matching Section 3.4.

verification.spec: Import the Quest attention config/class and assert a parameter named like `num_skip_layers` (or synonym documented in config) exists and its default value equals 2; grep the code path applying Quest to confirm it skips exactly this many initial layers.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that transformer layers with index < num_skip_layers execute the full dense FlashInfer attention path with the entire KV cache.

verification.spec: Spy on the dense FlashInfer attention path. Run a decode step through a mock 4-layer model with num_skip_layers=2. Assert that for layer_idx in {0, 1} the dense attention path is invoked with the FULL KV cache (all pages, not sparse indices) — verify the K/V arguments have the full token count.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that transformer layers with index >= num_skip_layers dispatch through the Quest two-stage sparse attention operator during decoding.

verification.spec: Spy on the Quest two-stage operator. Run a decode step through a mock 4-layer model with num_skip_layers=2. Assert the Quest operator is invoked exactly for layer_idx in {2, 3} and not for layer_idx in {0, 1}.

sub_tasks.requirements: Behavioral and structural claims tied specifically to this operator's design points from Sections 3.4 and 3.5 are directly verified.

A test verifies that on a synthetic input with known highest per-page attention masses, the Top-K page indices selected by Stage 1 (using true min/max Key metadata) contain the pages with the true Top-K attention masses when K is at least as large as the number of critical pages.

verification.spec: Construct a synthetic paged KV cache with N pages where a known subset of C pages contain Key vectors that yield the highest per-page attention masses w.r.t. a chosen Query. Compute true per-page max attention mass via full scaled-dot-product attention grouped by page. Run Quest Stage 1 (using true element-wise min/max Key metadata) and select Top-K page indices with K >= C. Assert the returned Top-K set is a superset of the C ground-truth critical pages across multiple randomized trials.

sub_tasks.requirements: A test verifies that the operator's default configuration matches Section 3.4/3.5: page size = 16 and num_skip_layers = 2, and that these defaults are the ones used to reproduce the paper's accuracy tables.

verification.spec: Import the Quest operator/config module and assert the default page_size == 16 and num_skip_layers == 2. Additionally, inspect the reproduce.sh / eval scripts to confirm those defaults are passed (or unset, falling back to defaults) for the accuracy evaluations.

sub_tasks.requirements: The three CUDA kernels — criticality estimation, batched Top-K filtering via RAFT, and approximate PageAttention built on FlashInfer — are implemented, callable from the inference framework, and produce numerically correct outputs matching the reference algorithm.

The Quest kernel path depends on and correctly integrates FlashInfer (as the base sparse/paged attention library) and RAFT (as the batched Top-K source), and organizes the three CUDA kernel implementations in a discoverable module layout.

Code has been implemented that adds FlashInfer as a build/runtime dependency of the Quest kernel package (submodule, pip requirement, or pinned CMake reference) so FlashInfer PageAttention primitives are linkable from Quest's CUDA extension.

verification.spec: Inspect the Quest package's setup.py / pyproject.toml / requirements.txt / CMakeLists.txt / .gitmodules for a declared FlashInfer dependency (pip requirement 'flashinfer', git submodule, or CMake target). Additionally verify the Quest CUDA extension source files include or link against FlashInfer headers (grep for 'flashinfer' includes in csrc/).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that pulls in NVIDIA RAFT (specifically its batched Top-K CUDA primitive from `raft::matrix::select_k`) as a dependency of Quest's Top-K filtering kernel, either as a git submodule, header-only include, or linked library.

verification.spec: Inspect the Quest build configuration for a RAFT dependency: either .gitmodules referencing rapidsai/raft, a CMake FetchContent/find_package for raft, or explicit include of raft/matrix/select_k.cuh in the Top-K kernel source. Grep the Top-K wrapper .cu/.cuh files for 'raft::matrix::select_k' or equivalent usage.

sub_tasks.requirements: For each channel i the kernel computes `U_i = max(Q_i * m_i, Q_i * M_i)` (element-wise product with min and max Keys followed by per-channel max), exactly reproducing the upper-bound formulation regardless of the sign of `Q_i`.

verification.spec: Construct known Q, m, M vectors with mixed signs; call the criticality kernel; verify per-channel outputs equal max(Q_i * m_i, Q_i * M_i) elementwise within fp16/fp32 tolerance, including negative-Q cases where Q*m > Q*M.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that reduces the per-channel `U_i` values by summation across `head_dim` (typically via warp/block reduction) to produce a single scalar criticality score per (page, head).

verification.spec: Feed the criticality estimation kernel deterministic Q, page_min, page_max tensors of shape [pages, heads, head_dim] where the expected U_i = max(q*min, q*max) is analytically computable. verification.spec: Call the criticality kernel with random FP16 Q, page-min, page-max tensors on GPU; independently compute reference via `(Q.unsqueeze(-2) * torch.stack([mins,maxs],-2)).max(-2).values.sum(-1)`; assert element-wise max absolute error < 5e-2 * abs(reference).max().

sub_tasks.requirements: The kernel translates each `topk_indices[h, k]` entry into a page-table lookup and gathers only that page's K/V rows into shared memory / registers, so total K/V HBM reads are `2 * M * K * S` bytes per head, matching the Section 3.5 memory-movement formula.
